also: put out food for the birds

terms.gloss: a small trough: a bird feeder
evidence: Col. 8.3.8: aut aquā replentur aut cibō plumbeī canālēs
terms.comment: Columella’s word for the little troughs kept full of millet for the thrushes in an aviary; for hens, troughs of lead filled with water or food (canālēs). Lewis & Short gives the word as a small channel or pipe; its use for a garden feeder for wild birds is modern, and ours. Morgan–Owens has the heading “bird-feeder” with no word.

phrases.latin: Canāliculum miliō replē; avēs mox venient.
phrases.english: Fill the bird feeder with millet; the birds will soon come.
Look, a tit has flown to the feeder!

phrases.latin: Semper tamen etiam canāliculī miliō replētī adpōnuntur, quae est firmissima ēsca
phrases.english: But little troughs filled with millet, which is the most sustaining food, are always set out as well

sources: Lewis & Short: canaliculus · Lewis & Short: canalis · Lewis & Short: milium
